events.title: Early Bengali Civilization
events.description: Early settled civilizations emerged in Bengal region. Fertile Ganges Delta lands nurtured agricultural society. Ancestor languages of Bengali began forming.

events.title: Magadha Kingdom Rule
events.description: Indian Magadha Kingdom extended influence to Bengal region. Buddhism spread in this area.

events.title: Mauryan Empire Rule
events.description: Mauryan Empire under Ashoka controlled Bengal, Buddhism flourished. Multiple Buddhist sites still exist today.

events.title: Gupta Dynasty Golden Age
events.description: During Gupta dynasty rule, Bengal became Indian cultural and academic center. Sanskrit literature and art flourished.

events.title: Pala Dynasty and Buddhist Revival
events.description: Native Bengali Pala dynasty ruled, promoting Mahayana Buddhism. Nalanda University and Vikramashila became world Buddhist academic centers.

events.title: Muslim Conquest of Bengal
events.description: Delhi Sultanate conquered Bengal, Islam began spreading in Bengal. Large numbers of locals (especially low-caste Hindus) converted to Islam.

events.title: Bengal Sultanate
events.description: Independent Bengal Sultanate ruled Bengal, this was Bengal's first independent Muslim state. Capital Dhaka prospered.

events.title: Mughal Empire Conquers Bengal
events.description: Mughal Empire conquered Bengal, incorporating it into empire. Bengal became one of empire's wealthiest provinces.

events.title: Bengali Economic Prosperity
events.description: Bengal's textile industry (especially cotton and silk) world-famous, exported to Europe and Southeast Asia. Dhaka called 'Venice of the East.' Bengal accounted for 50% of Mughal Empire GDP.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.description: British East India Company defeated Bengal Nawab at Battle of Plassey, beginning to establish colonial rule in Bengal. This was key turning point in British conquest of India.

events.title: Great Bengal Famine
events.description: During early British rule, Bengal suffered great famine, about 10 million people (1/3 of population) starved to death. This was beginning of disastrous consequences of British colonial rule.

events.title: Partition of Bengal (First)
events.description: Britain divided Bengal into West Bengal (Hindu majority) and East Bengal (Muslim majority). Sparked strong opposition from Indian nationalist movement, partition revoked in 1911.

events.title: All-India Muslim League Founded
events.description: All-India Muslim League founded in Dhaka, later became main political force for Pakistan's establishment.

events.title: Bengal Famine
events.description: During WWII, British colonial policies and Japanese occupation of Burma led to another Bengal famine, killing about 3 million. British government's inadequate response condemned.

events.title: Partition of India and Division of Bengal
events.description: British India partitioned, Bengal divided into West Bengal (to India) and East Bengal (to Pakistan, called East Pakistan). Mass population migrations and religious violence caused tragic casualties.

events.title: East Pakistan Period
events.description: East Bengal became East Pakistan, 1,600 km from West Pakistan. Though East Pakistanis had larger population, they were discriminated against politically, economically, and militarily by West Pakistan-dominated central government.

events.title: Language Movement
events.description: East Pakistani students protested against Pakistani government's imposition of Urdu as sole national language, demanding recognition of Bengali. Police opened fire, killing several students. This marked the beginning of the Bengali nationalist movement. February 21 later became International Mother Language Day.

events.title: Bhola Cyclone Disaster
events.description: Super cyclone struck East Pakistan, killing about 300,000-500,000, the deadliest cyclone on record. Pakistani government's slow response intensified East Pakistani discontent.

events.title: General Election and Awami League Victory
events.description: Pakistan's first democratic general election, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman-led East Pakistani Awami League won absolute majority (won 160 of 167 National Assembly seats). But West Pakistani military and politicians refused to transfer power.

events.title: Mujib's Historic Speech
events.description: Sheikh Mujib delivered speech to million people in Dhaka, calling 'This struggle is for freedom, this struggle is for independence,' sparking independence movement climax.

events.title: Operation Searchlight and Independence Declaration
events.description: Pakistani military launched Operation Searchlight, brutally suppressing East Pakistani people, massacring civilians, students, and intellectuals. Mujib arrested after declaring independence. Genocide began.

events.title: Bangladesh Liberation War and Genocide
events.description: Pakistani military committed genocide, killing about 3-30 million people (mostly civilians), raping 200,000-400,000 women, causing 10 million refugees to flee to India. Mukti Bahini guerrillas fought valiantly.

events.title: Indian Intervention and Pakistani Surrender
events.description: India declared war on Pakistan, Indian forces and Mukti Bahini jointly attacked. December 16, Pakistani military surrendered in Dhaka, 93,000 Pakistani troops became POWs.

events.title: Bangladesh Independence
events.description: People's Republic of Bangladesh officially became independent. December 16 became Bangladesh's 'Victory Day,' the most important national holiday.

events.title: Mujib Returns Home
events.description: Sheikh Mujib, imprisoned by Pakistan, released and returned home to hero's welcome. He became Bangladesh's first Prime Minister, revered as 'Bangabandhu' (Father of the Nation).

events.title: Constitution and Parliamentary Democracy
events.description: Bangladesh adopted constitution, establishing parliamentary democracy with Mujib as Prime Minister. Four national principles: nationalism, socialism, democracy, secularism.

events.title: Famine
events.description: Bangladesh suffered severe famine, about 1.5 million people starved to death. Government response was criticized. This damaged Mujib government's reputation.

events.title: One-Party Dictatorship
events.description: Mujib amended constitution, banned all parties except his BAKSAL party, establishing authoritarian rule. Democratic experiment ended.

events.title: Mujib Assassinated
events.description: Young military officers staged coup, assassinating Mujib and most of his family at home. Only two daughters (including future PM Sheikh Hasina) survived abroad.

events.title: Military Coups and Ziaur Rahman
events.description: Series of military coups followed Mujib's assassination. General Ziaur Rahman (Zia) seized power, ruling until his assassination in 1981.

events.title: Ershad Military Dictatorship
events.description: General Ershad seized power through coup, ruling for 8 years. Corruption was rampant. Mass protests in 1990 forced him to resign.

events.title: Return to Democracy
events.description: Bangladesh held free elections, Khaleda Zia (Ziaur Rahman's widow) became Prime Minister. Parliamentary democracy restored. Since then, Bangladesh alternated between Khaleda's BNP and Sheikh Hasina's Awami League.

events.title: Great Famine
events.description: Floods and food shortages led to famine, killing about 1.5 million. Newborn Bangladesh faced severe crisis.

events.title: Assassination of Mujib
events.description: Military coup, 'Father of the Nation' Sheikh Mujib and his family (except two daughters abroad) assassinated by military officers. Bangladesh plunged into prolonged military dictatorship.

events.title: Ziaur Rahman Military Rule
events.description: General Ziaur Rahman seized power, overthrowing secularism, emphasizing Islamic identity. He founded Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

events.title: Assassination of Zia
events.description: President Ziaur Rahman assassinated in coup. His widow Khaleda Zia later inherited political legacy.

events.title: Ershad Military Coup
events.description: General Ershad launched coup, establishing military dictatorship, ruling until 1990. He further Islamized the state.

events.title: Democracy Movement Overthrows Ershad
events.description: Mass democracy movement forced Ershad to step down. Bangladesh restored democratic elections.

events.title: 'Two Ladies' Alternating Rule
events.description: Khaleda Zia (BNP) and Hasina Wajed (Awami League, Mujib's daughter), two former leaders' widows alternated in power. Two parties fiercely opposed, political violence frequent.

events.title: Great Cyclone Disaster
events.description: Super cyclone struck Bangladesh, killing about 140,000. Bangladesh is one of world's most vulnerable countries to climate disasters.

events.title: Flood Disaster
events.description: Bangladesh suffered severe flooding, 2/3 of country inundated, tens of millions affected. Flooding is perennial threat to Bangladesh.

events.title: Muhammad Yunus Wins Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: Bangladeshi economist Muhammad Yunus won Nobel Peace Prize for founding Grameen Bank and promoting microcredit, helping millions of poor women escape poverty.

events.title: Hasina's Prolonged Rule
events.description: Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League won election, beginning prolonged rule (2009-present). She promoted economic development, but democracy regressed, opposition suppressed.

events.title: War Crimes Trials
events.description: Bangladesh established International War Crimes Tribunal, trying war criminals from 1971 Liberation War (mostly Islamic party members). Many sentenced to death and executed.

events.title: Rana Plaza Collapse
events.description: Dhaka Rana Plaza garment factory building collapsed, killing over 1,100. This highlighted terrible labor conditions in Bangladesh garment industry (economic pillar), drawing international attention.

events.title: Dhaka Café Terror Attack
events.description: Islamic extremists attacked Dhaka Holey Artisan Café, taking hostages and killing 22 (mostly foreigners). This was Bangladesh's worst terror attack.

events.title: Rohingya Refugee Crisis
events.description: About 700,000 Rohingya Muslims fled Myanmar to Bangladesh, Bangladesh hosting over 1 million Rohingya refugees. This brought huge burden to impoverished Bangladesh.

events.title: Economic Growth and Challenges
events.description: Bangladesh economy rapidly grew (mainly from garment industry), transforming from 'basket case' to developing country model. But faces challenges including poverty, corruption, climate change, democratic regression. 170 million population makes it one of world's most densely populated countries.

events.title: Fall of Hasina Government
events.description: Massive student movement and public protests overthrew Hasina's 15-year rule. Hasina fled to India, interim government formed. Bangladesh politics entered a new period of uncertainty.

events.title: 哈西娜政權垮台
events.description: 大規模學生運動和民眾抗議推翻哈西娜長達15年的統治。哈西娜逃往印度，臨時政府成立。孟加拉政治進入新的不確定時期。...
